analysis: What changed vs the 5 AM brief: the bounce is still on but cooling into the open — S&P futures slipped from +2.70% to +2.2%, Nasdaq 100 from +3.48% to +3.0%, Dow from +1.88% to +1.6% (IBD, ~8:38 AM ET). On the sourced numbers, only Alphabet has reclaimed its Thursday close among the megacaps; the rest have recovered roughly half of Friday's drop (Nvidia -14% Friday vs +9% now; Tesla -7.6% vs +4.2%; Meta -5.9% vs +3.3%). The freshest genuine catalysts in the last hour are the confirmed CrowdStrike–Zscaler deal, Anthropic holding above $92 on day three, and a new caution flag from BCA Research that the market 'failed to find a floor' — the correction may be the start of something bigger. The VIX tension persists: spot VIX ~30 premarket (down from Friday's 35.89 close) while VIX futures run +10%, and Asia did not join the bounce (Kospi -3.3% despite Seoul's stabilization package). Signal vs noise: the M&A deal, the supplier-price-hike earnings checks (HPE tonight), and today's PMI are signal; the size of the premarket snapback is noise until the cash open, in a thin Thanksgiving-week tape. No qualifying HN or Reddit thread surfaced in the last hour.
breadth_notes: Prior session (Fri Nov 20): S&P -3.70% to 6,910.39, Nasdaq -5.28% to 22,617.73, Dow -1.93%; S&P and Dow confirmed in correction, more than 10% below record closing highs; 93% of US stocks fell Friday (thelattehq). headlines.headline: Futures cooling off their best levels into the open: S&P 500 +2.2%, Nasdaq 100 +3.0%, Dow +1.6% as of ~8:38 AM ET (IBD), down from +2.70%/+3.48%/+1.88% at 5:40 AM ET. SPY +2.2% and QQQ +3% premarket; Barron's has S&P futures +2.46% and Dow +1.87%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A third straight hour of green futures, but the fade from the highs shows dip-buying enthusiasm thinning before the bell — the cash open, not the premarket print, is the real test after the worst week since 2020.

headlines.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) +~9% premarket to ~$136 after Friday's 14% plunge; shares closed Friday more than 48% off their 52-week high, capping a seventh straight weekly loss — the longest weekly losing streak since 2008. Trump is still pressing the board to rehire Jensen Huang; the board said Nov 17 it does not intend to, and Bessent's Nov 25 deadline on shell companies plus the SEC accounting probe remain open.
headlines.why_it_matters: The biggest single-name driver of the bounce, but the move recovers only about half of Friday's drop and nothing about the board, the Nov 25 deadline, or the SEC probe has changed — sentiment and short-covering as much as substance.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) +4.1% to $92.59 premarket (Barron's) on its third day of public trading, after closing Friday at $88.91 (-8.5%), still above the $83 IPO price. The stock opened Thursday at $111.50 and touched $115 before giving most of it back.
headlines.why_it_matters: The newest mega-IPO is stabilizing above its offer price after a wild first two sessions — a small read-through for risk appetite, though the FT view (via CNBC) that bookrunners erred by not exercising the greenshoe is secondhand and unconfirmed.

headlines.headline: CrowdStrike (CRWD) to acquire Zscaler (ZS) in a confirmed $43.9B all-stock deal (1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share, ~34% premium to Friday's close). CrowdStrike -8% premarket, Zscaler +19% (IBD; Barron's has ZS +17.8%). Kymera Therapeutics (KYMR) +29.4% premarket led Barron's mover board.
headlines.why_it_matters: The biggest cybersecurity deal ever, confirmed rather than rumored — M&A is still moving through the drawdown, and the market is charging the buyer (CRWD -8%) while paying the target a full premium.

headlines.headline: Megacaps broadly higher premarket: Alphabet (GOOGL) +5.1% and Amazon (AMZN) +3.1% (IBD); Meta +3.25% to $579.07, Microsoft +2.70% to $497.58, Apple +1.01% to $346.03, Tesla +4.22% to $360.40 (Finnhub, 8:53 AM ET). Chip breadth is strong too: SOXX +5% and the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) +8% premarket (Investopedia).
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound is broad, not just Nvidia — but on the sourced numbers only Alphabet is back above its Thursday close, so most megacaps are still well underwater from Friday's rout.

headlines.headline: BCA Research warned this morning that the market 'failed to find a floor, raising the question of whether this correction is the start of something bigger' — even after Nvidia's earnings beat and Anthropic's IPO (Investopedia).
headlines.why_it_matters: A counterweight to the premarket euphoria from a named research house: if the bounce is just short-covering into a thin holiday week, the open could give it back fast.

usac.headline: USA Compression Partners completed its acquisition of J-W Power Company for approximately $860 million (announced Nov 22): $430M cash from its revolving credit facility plus ~18.2M common units at $23.50 each. The deal adds over 0.8M active horsepower across the Northeast, Mid-Continent, Rockies, Gulf Coast and Permian, taking the combined fleet to ~4.4M active horsepower.
usac.why_it_matters: The first material USAC company news in the brief cycle — a large, fleet-expanding acquisition that grows the horsepower base ~22%, though it was funded partly with new units and revolver debt, so leverage and dilution are the offsets to watch.

watch_next: S&P Global November Composite PMI due today at 9:45 AM ET — the first data read of the holiday-shortened week.
Whether the futures bounce holds into the 9:30 AM ET cash open and the VIX gets back below 30 — futures have already faded from their best levels, and VIX futures are up ~10% even as spot VIX falls.
Earnings after the close today: HPE, Agilent, Zoom — HPE is the first check on the reported supplier price hikes (FT: Dell, HPE, Supermicro hiking prices up to 45%).
Wednesday's data dump before Thanksgiving: core PCE (expected ~3.2% y/y), Q3 GDP, durable goods, jobless claims, Beige Book — the next real test for the near-certain December Fed hike.
Nvidia's response to Bessent's Nov 25 deadline on shell companies, and any board response to Trump's rehire push.
